title: Take Me With You
hookLine: Krishna is about to leave the world, and his friend asks for one thing: take me with you
carry: karma: keep acting, with your mind on krishna
tomorrow: a king asks a wanderer where his calm comes from.

lines: WHAT HE GETS INSTEAD: A TEACHING.
cards: Krishna is about to leave the world. In the Bhagavata's eleventh book, the gods come to remind him that his work on earth is done, and his own clan is heading toward its end.

Uddhava hears it: his close friend, the learned messenger who once carried his words to Vraja. He comes to Krishna alone and asks for one thing: take me with you. He says he can't bear to be apart from him.
What Krishna gives him instead is a long teaching. Tradition calls it the Uddhava Gita.

teach.h: DON'T FOLLOW ME. LET GO, AND WANDER.
teach.b: Krishna's first answer sounds hard. Don't follow me, he says. When I'm gone, let go of your attachment to family and friends, fix your mind on me, and wander the earth seeing everything evenly.

teach.h: THIS IS HARD FOR ME. TEACH ME HOW.
teach.b: In effect he says: this kind of letting go is hard for people like me, whose minds cling to the body and to what is ours. Teach me how. And Krishna does, chapter after chapter, before he goes.
That's the shape of the whole Uddhava Gita: an honest question, and a teacher who stays to answer it. Why read it on the path of action? Back on day seven, karma meant action itself, not payback.
And Uddhava isn't a sage in a cave. He's a man with duties, a household, a city, and a friend about to be gone.

teach.h: THE KARMA QUESTION: HOW DO I KEEP ACTING?
teach.b: His question is the karma question: how do I keep acting in a world that keeps losing things?
The next few days come at it from several sides: what to learn from the people who wrong you, which path suits whom, where joy and sorrow really come from, and how to work without hurry.
And notice: Krishna doesn't take Uddhava with him. The teacher leaves, and the student keeps living.
That's the teaching under the whole book, karma yoga in Krishna's last words: keep acting in the world, with your mind fixed on God, even after the one you leaned on is gone.

how: Students of the Bhagavata Purana read the eleventh book's long dialogue between Krishna and Uddhava, known as the Uddhava Gita, as a teaching in its own right, and it is recited along with the rest of the Purana when the whole text is read aloud.

action: the work you do, the deed itself

p: let go, and wander, mind fixed on me

s: Krishna takes Uddhava with him when he leaves the world
he tells Uddhava to stay, let go and wander, and then teaches him at length.
Uddhava says the first teaching is easy to follow
he says letting go is hard for someone whose mind clings, and asks to be taught how.
Uddhava is the same friend who once carried Krishna's words to Vraja
the learned messenger of the tenth book returns as the questioner of the eleventh.

games.q: you're Uddhava. your friend Krishna is about to leave the world. what do you ask him for?
o: a kingdom to look after once he's gone.
to be taken along with him.
games.why: Uddhava asks to go with him. Krishna says no, and then stays to teach him. that teaching is the Uddhava Gita.

practice: Bring to mind someone who taught you something and isn't here to ask anymore, a grandparent, a teacher, a friend who moved away, and instead of reaching for the loss, reach for one thing they left you: a habit, a saying, a way of doing an ordinary job.

Hold that one thing, and if you pray, offer that person and that gift to the One you pray to. If a loss feels too heavy to hold alone, please reach out: in the US, call or text 988, or your local emergency number.

wordCard.voice: Karma. Action, work, the deed itself. In the Uddhava Gita it begins with one honest question: how to keep acting when the one you leaned on is leaving.

orig.note: Sanskrit: action, work, deed. the path of karma is the path of action.

carryVoice: Your line: karma, keep acting, with your mind on Krishna. What the teacher left is what you work with now. Back tomorrow, same hill.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 11.6 (the gods ask Krishna to return; Uddhava comes to him privately and asks to be taken along)
Bhagavata Purana 11.7.1–18 (Krishna tells Uddhava to give up attachment and wander with his mind on him; Uddhava says this is hard and asks to be taught)
Bhagavata Purana 10.46–47 (Uddhava as messenger to Vraja, recalled)
